title: GRADE 10 - UNIT 2 - PRACTICE FOR 15' TEST - EXERCISE 4

cards.front: 1. This shirt looks beautiful. I _____ it.
cards.explanation:
✓ C. will buy.

This is a decision made at the moment of speaking after seeing the shirt. We commonly use “will” for an instant decision.

A. am buying = present continuous, usually for an arranged future
B. buy = present simple
C. will buy = will + V, suitable for an instant decision
D. buys = present simple, third-person singular

cards.front: 2. I have made a reservation. We _____ dinner at the Hoa Sua restaurant nearby.
cards.explanation:
✓ A. are going to have.

“I have made a reservation” shows a prior plan/intention, so “be going to” is appropriate.

A. are going to have = planned future, subject “we”
B. will have = possible future, but less suitable for a pre-arranged plan here
C. have = present simple
D. is going to have = wrong subject–verb agreement with “we”

cards.front: 3. The Sun is shining. It _____ a lovely day.
cards.explanation:
✓ D. is going to be.

There is present evidence: “The Sun is shining.” We use “be going to” for a prediction based on what we can see now.

A. are = wrong with subject “It”
B. is = describes present state, not this future prediction
C. is being = present continuous form, not suitable here
D. is going to be = evidence-based prediction

cards.front: 4. Stop making so much noise or the neighbour _____ angry.
cards.explanation:
✓ B. will get.

This is a warning about a likely future consequence: “Stop ... or ... will ...”.

A. get = bare verb, not correct here
B. will get = future consequence
C. is going to get = possible in other contexts, but “or + will” is the natural warning pattern here
D. is getting = action/state happening now

cards.front: 5. She doesn't like Kate, so she _____ her to her house.
cards.explanation:
✓ B. isn’t going to invite.

Her dislike of Kate suggests an intention/plan not to invite her, so “be going to” fits.

A. is going to invite = opposite meaning
B. isn’t going to invite = planned/intended negative future
C. will invite = opposite meaning
D. won't invite = possible as a prediction/refusal, but the sentence points to intention

cards.front: 6. I'm sure John _____ very happy to meet you.
cards.explanation:
✓ D. will be.

“I’m sure” is a common signal for a future prediction/opinion with “will”.

A. is = present
B. are = wrong agreement with “John”
C. is going to be = usually prediction based on present evidence
D. will be = prediction/opinion

cards.front: 7. She _____ the phone no matter who calls her.
cards.explanation:
✓ A. will not answer.

“No matter who calls her” expresses a firm future refusal/decision. “will not” is suitable.

A. will not answer = future refusal/decision
B. isn’t going to answer = planned intention; possible in some contexts but less direct here
C. answers = present simple
D. is answering = action happening now

cards.front: 8. You _____ able to see much better with these new glasses.
cards.explanation:
✓ C. will be.

This is a prediction about the result of using the new glasses.

A. are = present, changes the intended meaning
B. is = wrong agreement with “you”
C. will be = future prediction/result
D. are going to be = possible in some contexts, but “will be able to” is the standard form here

cards.front: 9. I don't think he _____ that car because it's old and unreliable.
cards.explanation:
✓ B. will get.

“I don’t think ...” commonly introduces a future prediction with “will”.

A. is getting = arranged/present continuous future
B. will get = prediction/opinion
C. is going to get = prior intention/plan or evidence-based future
D. gets = present simple

cards.front: 10. Look at the child's face. He _____.
cards.explanation:
✓ A. is going to cry.

“Look at the child’s face” provides present evidence for a prediction. Use “be going to”.

A. is going to cry = evidence-based prediction
B. cries = present simple / habit
C. will cry = prediction without the same emphasis on present evidence
D. is crying = means the crying is already happening

cards.front: 11. She aims at _____ the Environment Club to clean up our environment with other people.
cards.explanation:
✓ D. joining.

Structure: aim at + noun / V-ing.
→ “aims at joining”.

A. join = bare verb
B. to join = infinitive; not used after the preposition “at” here
C. joined = past/V3
D. joining = V-ing after “at”

cards.front: 12. The best solution is to raise people’s _____ of environmental issues and the effects of pollution.
cards.explanation:
✓ B. awareness = nhận thức.

WORD FAMILY:
A. aware (adj) = nhận thức được
B. awareness (n) = nhận thức
C. unaware (adj) = không nhận thức được
D. unawareness (n) = sự thiếu nhận thức

Collocation: “raise awareness of/about something”.

cards.front: 13. _____ your appliances when they are not in use is one of the easiest ways to save energy.
cards.explanation:
✓ A. Turning off = việc tắt.

CÁC LỰA CHỌN:
A. turn off = tắt
B. turn on = bật
C. turn up = vặn to / tăng mức
D. turn down = vặn nhỏ / giảm mức

The V-ing phrase acts as the subject. To save energy, we turn appliances off when not in use.

cards.front: 14. We should encourage people to use _____ bottles to reduce plastic waste.
cards.explanation:
✓ C. refillable = có thể nạp/làm đầy lại.

CÁC LỰA CHỌN:
A. renewable = có thể tái tạo
B. remarkable = đáng chú ý; nổi bật
C. refillable = có thể châm đầy lại
D. resolved = đã được giải quyết / kiên quyết

“refillable bottles” are bottles that can be filled and used again, helping reduce plastic waste.

cards.front: 15. Children should be taught how to sort and recycle household items instead of _____ them.
cards.explanation:
✓ D. throwing away = vứt bỏ.

CÁC LỰA CHỌN:
A. cut down = cắt giảm
B. clean up = dọn dẹp
C. break down = phân hủy / hỏng
D. throw away = vứt đi

Structure: instead of + V-ing. The meaning contrasts recycling with throwing items away.
